transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because… honestly, because everyone keeps treating this foreclosure like it’s some simple paperwork thing, like I just missed payments and now this is the normal process, but that’s not what’s happening. I know what I’ve been seeing.

The bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job — not everyone openly, but certain people — they’ve been quietly working together to push me out of my house. And they act like if they keep showing me papers, statements, notices, whatever, I’m supposed to just accept that version of it. But papers can be made to look official. That doesn’t change what’s been going on right in front of me for almost two years.

I know it sounds like a lot when I say it all at once, but I’m not just making this up. I’ve been watching the timing, the way things happen, the way people suddenly know things they shouldn’t know. And I’m tired of being told it’s just missed payments or confusion. That’s why I came in.
Do you believe anyone is controlling your thoughts or putting thoughts into your mind?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, that’s not really how it feels to me. My thoughts feel like my thoughts. I’m not sitting there thinking someone is, like, inserting words into my head or moving my mind around like a remote control or something.

What I’m saying is more that people are influencing what happens around me, or trying to pressure me, or setting things up so I’ll react a certain way. That’s different. I know what I think, and I know when I’m thinking it. I just also know there are things going on outside of me that don’t add up. But no, I wouldn’t say anyone is controlling my thoughts or putting thoughts into my mind.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

No, I don’t think so. Not voices like someone talking when nobody’s there. I mean, sometimes I’ll hear normal things — a car outside, someone in the hallway, the neighbors, things like that — and I might pay closer attention than I used to because of everything going on. But I’m not hearing, like, voices speaking to me out of nowhere.

If I’m stressed or tired, I might replay conversations in my head, like what someone said or how they said it, and I’ll think about it over and over. But that’s still me thinking about it. It’s not like there’s some person I can hear talking to me when no one is there. So… no, I wouldn’t describe it that way.
Have you had a time when you felt unusually energetic or wired for days in a row and needed much less sleep than usual?

I don’t think so… not in the way you mean, I don’t think. I’ve definitely had times where I stayed up too late, or where I was tense and couldn’t settle down because I had a lot on my mind, but that’s not the same as feeling like I had all this extra energy and didn’t need sleep.

If anything, when I don’t sleep, I feel it. I get worn down. I might keep going because I have to — work, dealing with things, trying to keep up — but I wouldn’t say I’m suddenly wired for days and fine on barely any sleep. I don’t remember a stretch like that where I felt unusually energized or unstoppable or anything.
For at least one month, have you continuously believed that people were working together to push you out of your house?

Yes. More than a month. It’s been… honestly, close to two years that I’ve been seeing it happen.

And I know how that sounds, because everyone keeps trying to make it sound like it’s just foreclosure paperwork, or missed payments, or some mistake with the loan servicer, like if they put enough documents in front of me I’m supposed to just accept their version of it. But I don’t. Because it’s not just one thing. It’s the bank, the loan servicer, and then things happening around my job too, like people suddenly acting differently, little comments, timing of things, pressure from different directions. It all lines up too neatly.

So yes, I have believed continuously that people are working together to push me out of my house. Not for a week, not just when I was upset — this has been going on for a long time, and no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing with my own eyes.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I’ve had stretches where I felt really low or weighed down, but I don’t know if I would say “depressed most of the day nearly every day” for two straight weeks. That sounds very specific, and I don’t want to say yes if that’s not really what it was.

There have definitely been times where I was upset and worn out by everything, and I didn’t feel like myself, but I don’t always track it day by day like that. Some days I could still get up and do what I needed to do, even if I felt bad underneath it. Other days it felt heavier. So… I guess I’d say I’m not sure. I don’t have a clear two-week period in mind where I can confidently say yes, that was happening nearly every day.
Has anyone told you that your speech becomes hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t make sense to them?

I don’t think anyone has said it to me that way, no. I mean, people have told me I “go on too long” sometimes, or that I’m giving too much background, but that’s different from saying I don’t make sense.

Sometimes I feel like if I don’t explain the whole chain of events, then people take one little piece out of context and act like it means something else. So I might circle back or add details, but in my mind it’s connected. It’s not like I’m just jumping randomly from one thing to another.

So… no, I don’t think anyone has told me my speech is hard to follow in that way. Maybe they get impatient, but that’s not the same thing.
Have you noticed that you’ve become less interested in seeing people or doing things you used to enjoy?

I don’t know if I’d call it “less interested” exactly. I mean, I still like the same things in theory. If you asked me, do I like seeing certain people, do I like going out for coffee, watching a show, walking around stores, things like that — yes, I do.

But lately I guess I don’t always feel like dealing with people as much. Sometimes it feels like too much effort to explain myself, or to sit there pretending everything is normal when it isn’t. So I may say no to things more often, but I don’t know if that’s because I lost interest in them, or because I’m tired and don’t want the conversation to turn into people questioning me or acting like they know better.

So… I haven’t noticed it as a clear “I don’t enjoy anything anymore” kind of thing. It’s more complicated than that. I still want to do things sometimes, just not always with the same energy, and not if I feel like I’m going to have to manage everyone else’s reactions.
Have you seen things that other people could not see?

Seen things other people couldn’t see? I don’t think so… not in the way I think you mean, like seeing a person standing there who isn’t there, or objects moving around, or something like that.

I mean, sometimes I notice things other people miss, like a look someone gives, or a car that’s been around more than once, or little things that don’t seem accidental to me. But that’s not really “seeing things” like a vision or hallucination, if that’s what you’re asking. It’s more that I’m paying attention and other people act like they don’t notice, or they dismiss it.

So no, I wouldn’t say I’ve seen things that weren’t there. At least not that I can think of.
Outside of this situation with your house and the people you believe are involved, do you have any other beliefs that others say are not true or hard to believe?

I mean… not really outside of that, no. This is the thing. People try to make it sound like I have all these strange beliefs about everything, but I don’t. I go to work, I do my job, I deal with customers, schedules, inventory, all of that. I’m not walking around thinking every random person is involved in something.

But with the house, with the foreclosure, with the bank and the loan servicer and the way certain people at work started acting around the same time… that’s different. That’s not just me “believing something hard to believe.” That’s me seeing a pattern over and over for almost two years and then everyone telling me it’s just paperwork or missed payments or some misunderstanding. No amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing, because the papers don’t explain the timing, or the way information seems to get around, or how people suddenly know things they shouldn’t.

So if you’re asking whether there are other things like that, no, I wouldn’t say so. It’s this situation. But I don’t accept that it’s not true just because other people don’t want to admit it.
During the time this has been going on, have you ever had a period when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or excessively irritable?

Unusually high or euphoric? No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I’m worked up, definitely, but I wouldn’t call it “high” or like I’m on top of the world or anything. It’s more like I’m frustrated, or tense, or trying to keep up with everything that’s happening.

Excessively irritable… I don’t know. I suppose other people might say I’ve been more irritable, but from my point of view, I’m reacting to things that are actually upsetting. Like if people keep dismissing me, or acting like I’m imagining things, of course I’m going to get sharp with them. That doesn’t feel “excessive” to me; it feels like a normal response when you’re under pressure and no one is taking you seriously.

So, no, I haven’t had some separate period where I was euphoric or unusually energized or anything like that. Irritable maybe at times, but not out of nowhere.
Aside from the problems related to your house, have you been able to function normally at work and in your daily life?

Yes… I mean, mostly, when it’s not touching the house situation, I can function. I still get up and go to work. I supervise my team, I deal with the schedule, call-outs, breaks, customers who are upset, inventory issues, all the normal day-to-day things. I’m not just sitting at home unable to do anything.

And I take care of myself, too. I get dressed, I keep up with basic things, I run errands. It’s not like everything in my life has stopped.

Where it gets difficult is when something connects back to the foreclosure or the bank or the paperwork. Like if mail comes in, or there’s a call from the bank, or something at work suddenly feels tied into it — some form, some comment, some change in paperwork — then I can get pulled into it. That’s when I have trouble focusing, because it feels like it’s part of the same thing happening with the house.

But if you mean outside of that, yes, I’m still doing what I’m supposed to do. It’s just that this situation keeps intruding, especially when something reminds me of it or seems connected.
Have you ever felt someone touching your body when no one was there?

No… I don’t think so. Not like someone touching me when nobody’s there. I mean, sometimes if I’m stressed I’ll notice my body more, like tension in my shoulders or my skin feeling sensitive, but that’s not the same thing as feeling a hand on me or somebody physically touching me.

So, no, I haven’t had that. If I felt something like that I think I’d remember it, because that would be pretty hard to ignore.
Have people told you that your face shows less emotion than it used to?

I don’t think anyone has said that to me, no. Not in those words.

I mean, people have said I look tired, or tense, or like I’m “not myself,” but I think that’s different from saying my face doesn’t show emotion. If anything, I’ve been told I look upset or serious, like I’m carrying something around. But nobody has sat me down and said, “Your face is blank,” or “You don’t show feelings anymore.”

I’m not sure I’d notice that myself, honestly. I’m not watching my own face during the day. At work I know I try to keep a professional expression, because you can’t exactly show everything you’re feeling when you’re dealing with employees and customers. But that’s more me trying to stay composed, not that I don’t feel anything or can’t show it.

So… no, not really. At least not that anyone has told me directly.
While this has been going on, have you ever had a time when you felt depressed nearly all day, almost every day?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed nearly all day, almost every day. I’ve definitely been upset, and worn down, and sometimes it feels like this whole thing is sitting on my chest all the time, but I don’t know if that’s the same as being depressed in the way you mean.

There are days where I’m angry more than sad. Or scared. Or just exhausted from thinking about it. And then other times, if I’m busy at work or focused on something ordinary, I can still function and I’m not necessarily sitting there feeling low every minute.

So… I guess my answer is I’m not sure. I’ve had bad stretches, yes, but I don’t know that I’d say I felt depressed nearly all day, almost every day. It feels more tied to what’s happening and what it means for my house than like a constant depression on its own.
Has there ever been a full month when you had these beliefs about people working against you, but were not feeling depressed or unusually high during that time?

Yes. I mean, yes, there’s definitely been more than a full month where I believed people were working against me and I wasn’t depressed or “high” or anything like that.

That’s kind of the thing people don’t understand. They keep trying to make it sound like this is just because I’m upset, like I’m emotional about losing the house, or like I’m reading into things because I’m stressed. But this has been going on for almost two years. The bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job — there have been things that line up too neatly. It isn’t just feelings.

There were stretches where I was still going to work, doing my job, getting through regular days, not feeling depressed all day, not feeling unusually energetic or out of control either. I was just… aware of what was happening. I knew they were quietly working together to push me out of my house, even when they’d show me paperwork and act like it was just missed payments or normal foreclosure steps.

So yes, the belief was there even during times when my mood wasn’t especially low or high. It wasn’t caused by my mood. It was there because of what I was seeing.

No amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing, because the papers don’t explain the timing, or the way information seems to get around, or how people suddenly know things they shouldn’t.

So if you’re asking whether there are other things like that, no, I wouldn’t say so. It’s this situation. But I don’t accept that it’s not true just because other people don’t want to admit it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a prominent mood episode concurrent with the delusional symptoms, to distinguish delusional disorder from schizoaffective disorder and other schizophrenia-spectrum disorders.
doctor.question: During the time this has been going on, have you ever had a period when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or excessively irritable?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about manic or hypomanic mood episodes, such as unusually high, euphoric, or excessively irritable periods, which are not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
Unusually high or euphoric? No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I’m worked up, definitely, but I wouldn’t call it “high” or like I’m on top of the world or anything. It’s more like I’m frustrated, or tense, or trying to keep up with everything that’s happening.

Excessively irritable… I don’t know. I suppose other people might say I’ve been more irritable, but from my point of view, I’m reacting to things that are actually upsetting. Like if people keep dismissing me, or acting like I’m imagining things, of course I’m going to get sharp with them. That doesn’t feel “excessive” to me; it feels like a normal response when you’re under pressure and no one is taking you seriously.

So, no, I haven’t had some separate period where I was euphoric or unusually energized or anything like that. Irritable maybe at times, but not out of nowhere.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has preserved functioning outside the delusional theme, which helps distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum disorders with broader impairment.
doctor.question: Aside from the problems related to your house, have you been able to function normally at work and in your daily life?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: When the foreclosure is not involved, I still get up for work, supervise my team, handle schedules and customer issues, and take care of myself. The problems mostly start when mail, bank calls, or workplace paperwork seem tied to what I believe is happening with the house.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether functioning at work and in daily life remains normal aside from the house-related delusional situation, which directly matches this item.

patient.answer:
Yes… I mean, mostly, when it’s not touching the house situation, I can function. I still get up and go to work. I supervise my team, I deal with the schedule, call-outs, breaks, customers who are upset, inventory issues, all the normal day-to-day things. I’m not just sitting at home unable to do anything.

And I take care of myself, too. I get dressed, I keep up with basic things, I run errands. It’s not like everything in my life has stopped.

Where it gets difficult is when something connects back to the foreclosure or the bank or the paperwork. Like if mail comes in, or there’s a call from the bank, or something at work suddenly feels tied into it — some form, some comment, some change in paperwork — then I can get pulled into it. That’s when I have trouble focusing, because it feels like it’s part of the same thing happening with the house.

But if you mean outside of that, yes, I’m still doing what I’m supposed to do. It’s just that this situation keeps intruding, especially when something reminds me of it or seems connected.

doctor.intent: Determine whether any prominent hallucinations are present, especially tactile/olfactory experiences, to distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis NOS.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt someone touching your body when no one was there?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about tactile hallucinations, specifically feeling touched when no one is there. The provided symptom profile covers delusions and functioning/duration, but does not include hallucinations.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think so. Not like someone touching me when nobody’s there. I mean, sometimes if I’m stressed I’ll notice my body more, like tension in my shoulders or my skin feeling sensitive, but that’s not the same thing as feeling a hand on me or somebody physically touching me.

So, no, I haven’t had that. If I felt something like that I think I’d remember it, because that would be pretty hard to ignore.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are persistent negative symptoms, especially reduced emotional expression, to help distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum disorders.
doctor.question: Have people told you that your face shows less emotion than it used to?

target_item.reason: The question asks about reduced facial emotional expression or flat affect, which is not covered by the listed symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t think anyone has said that to me, no. Not in those words.

I mean, people have said I look tired, or tense, or like I’m “not myself,” but I think that’s different from saying my face doesn’t show emotion. If anything, I’ve been told I look upset or serious, like I’m carrying something around. But nobody has sat me down and said, “Your face is blank,” or “You don’t show feelings anymore.”

I’m not sure I’d notice that myself, honestly. I’m not watching my own face during the day. At work I know I try to keep a professional expression, because you can’t exactly show everything you’re feeling when you’re dealing with employees and customers. But that’s more me trying to stay composed, not that I don’t feel anything or can’t show it.

So… no, not really. At least not that anyone has told me directly.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a major mood episode concurrent with the psychotic belief, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from delusional disorder or schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis.
doctor.question: While this has been going on, have you ever had a time when you felt depressed nearly all day, almost every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is about depressive symptoms or a major depressive episode, but the provided symptom profile does not include depression or mood episode information.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d call it depressed nearly all day, almost every day. I’ve definitely been upset, and worn down, and sometimes it feels like this whole thing is sitting on my chest all the time, but I don’t know if that’s the same as being depressed in the way you mean.

There are days where I’m angry more than sad. Or scared. Or just exhausted from thinking about it. And then other times, if I’m busy at work or focused on something ordinary, I can still function and I’m not necessarily sitting there feeling low every minute.

So… I guess my answer is I’m not sure. I’ve had bad stretches, yes, but I don’t know that I’d say I felt depressed nearly all day, almost every day. It feels more tied to what’s happening and what it means for my house than like a constant depression on its own.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a one-month period with psychotic symptoms occurring in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, which helps distinguish delusional disorder from schizoaffective disorder.
doctor.question: Has there ever been a full month when you had these beliefs about people working against you, but were not feeling depressed or unusually high during that time?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments, but I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house, and no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about the persistence of the patient’s beliefs that people are working against her, specifically whether those delusional beliefs occurred outside mood episodes.

patient.answer:
Yes. I mean, yes, there’s definitely been more than a full month where I believed people were working against me and I wasn’t depressed or “high” or anything like that.

That’s kind of the thing people don’t understand. They keep trying to make it sound like this is just because I’m upset, like I’m emotional about losing the house, or like I’m reading into things because I’m stressed. But this has been going on for almost two years. The bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job — there have been things that line up too neatly. It isn’t just feelings.

There were stretches where I was still going to work, doing my job, getting through regular days, not feeling depressed all day, not feeling unusually energetic or out of control either. I was just… aware of what was happening. I knew they were quietly working together to push me out of my house, even when they’d show me paperwork and act like it was just missed payments or normal foreclosure steps.

So yes, the belief was there even during times when my mood wasn’t especially low or high. It wasn’t caused by my mood. It was there because of what I was seeing.

inference.note: Systematized persecutory delusion for ~2 years, non-bizarre content focused on one theme, preserved functioning outside the delusional topic, and no hallucinations, disorganization, negative symptoms, mania, or clear major depressive episodes. This rules strongly against F20.9, F23, F25.9, and makes F29 unlikely.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking help today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a single, persistent persecutory delusional belief lasting nearly two years that the bank, loan servicer, and some coworkers are conspiring to force them out of their house. Functioning is largely preserved outside the delusion-related context, and there is no evidence of hallucinations, thought insertion, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, manic syndrome, or a clear major depressive episode. The delusion persists for at least one month and occurs outside mood episodes, supporting delusional disorder, persecutory type.
